title: Empirical Evaluation of a Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Pipeline: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt‑5‑mini on 400 Intent→Configuration Tasks
abstract: We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002) and executed a fully archived paired experiment that measured operational failures when applying LLM‑generated network configuration changes directly (Baseline) versus applying a deterministic syntax/policy validator with at most one deterministic LLM repair (Guarded). Using gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted NetOps adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) on 400 unique public/synthetic intents (paired Baseline/Guarded, shared_initial_candidate semantics), the run completed 800 episodes with no infrastructure failures. All 400 paired intents were operationally successful under both arms (n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The observed paired difference (Guarded − Baseline)=0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI 0.00–0.00; 10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p=1.0. Critically, the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one identical candidate per pair and the deterministic validator never rejected any shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0), so the Guarded pipeline was inert on this execution (no repair calls invoked). We release full archived artifacts and hashes (execution_manifest) and interpret these results as a reproducible boundary case that clarifies how generation semantics and task selection determine whether a validator can be empirically exercised.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations, but incorrect changes can cause reachability loss, policy violations, and outages. Systems papers therefore recommend generate→validate→repair pipelines and bounded, auditable repair budgets. However, there is little preregistered, artifact‑grounded evidence quantifying realistic failure rates and the protective value of lightweight automated validators under controlled conditions. Research question and contribution. We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002) and executed a paired experiment asking: what is the paired difference in operational failure proportion when LLM‑generated configuration changes are applied directly (Baseline) versus when a deterministic syntax/policy validator (with ≤1 deterministic LLM repair) is applied (Guarded)? Our contributions are: (1) a frozen preregistration and complete archival of prompts, provider traces, model outputs, validator logs, emulator scoring, and SHA‑256 manifests; (2) a transparent paired execution (400 intents → 800 episodes) that produced a reproducible boundary outcome (no validator rejects, no failures); and (3) a focused analysis and interpretation showing how generation semantics and task selection jointly determine whether a validator can be empirically exercised.
sections.related_work: Positioning. We build on two overlapping literatures: LLMs for NetOps/AIOps (survey and system reports) and generate→validate→repair approaches in IaC/program repair and RAG systems. Representative, verified sources that guided our design include the LLM‑NetOps survey (W4415071524), intent→configuration work (doi:10.1002/nem.2313), and verifier‑guided IaC repair papers (doi:10.2139/ssrn.6608518; W7124141852; W4401857375). Prior work motivates bounded repair budgets and verifier integration; our paper contributes a preregistered, reproducible paired testbed and an explicit artifact audit trail so null/degenerate outcomes can be interpreted scientifically.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002) was frozen before any model call and required: adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model=gpt‑5‑mini; task_count=400 unique intents; execution_mode=scientific_confirmatory; generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation=false); maximum_model_calls=800; maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1; paired Baseline vs Guarded design. The full preregistered plan and evidence list are archived (preregistration id CAND‑2026‑002; execution_manifest contains the preregistration SHA). Generation and application semantics. For each intent the system made a single shared generation call (gpt‑5‑mini) that produced one candidate configuration which was applied in Baseline. In Guarded that identical candidate was evaluated by a deterministic syntax/policy validator; on validator rejection a single deterministic LLM repair attempt was allowed (bounded). All prompts, generation templates, validator rules, and repair templates are archived (paths in execution_manifest). Execution environment and scoring. Emulated sandbox replicas executed changes and an automated scorer flagged operational failure (reachability loss or policy violation). Per‑task scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/*.json (see execution_manifest). Provenance and hashes. We archived every model/provider call, model output, validator decision log, scoring JSON, and the execution manifest with SHA‑256 hashes (notably: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf). Analysis plan. The primary estimand was the paired difference in operational failure proportion: P(failure|Baseline) − P(failure|Guarded) across 400 pairs. Confirmatory analysis used McNemar exact two‑sided test and 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed=1729). Secondary estimands (outage durations, rollbacks, vendor/change‑type subgroup rates) were preregistered for interpretation if failures occurred.

sections.discussion: Interpretation as a boundary case. The confirmatory statistics are numerically correct and fully reproducible from the archived artifacts. They constitute a boundary outcome: because generation_semantics was preregistered as shared_initial_candidate (one identical candidate per paired episode) and because the deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0), the Guarded intervention was inert for this execution — no repairs were invoked and no discordant outcomes were possible. Thus the run does not provide empirical evidence either that the validator improves safety or that it is unnecessary in general; it demonstrates that (A) generation semantics and (B) task selection jointly determine whether a validator can be empirically exercised. Design lessons for evaluators. To measure validator impact the evaluation must ensure the validator will have a nonzero expected firing frequency. Practical options (to be preregistered) include: (1) independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation=true) so Baseline and Guarded may apply different candidates; (2) injecting positive controls (intents that should be rejected by a correctly configured validator) to guarantee observed rejections; or (3) selecting a task bank with calibrated difficulty to provoke validator rejects at a nontrivial rate. Artifact‑grounded reviewer requests resolved. Per reviewer request we (i) expose validator decision logs and rules in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/transformation_manifest.json, (ii) provide exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 for principal numbers (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6...ab865; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887...), and (iii) publish representative prompt→shared candidate→validator pass→scorer JSON traces under execution/responses/* and execution/scoring/*.json. Sensitivity to scorer false negatives. We inspected preserved scoring JSONs; the archive contains no near‑failure or ambiguous scoring events, therefore the current artifacts cannot empirically demonstrate scorer/validator false negatives without newly injected failing inputs. This inability to resolve scorer sensitivity post hoc is an explicit limitation (see Limitations). External validity. This run used a single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single hosted adapter; emulator replicas and public/synthetic intents were used. Results do not generalize beyond these precise conditions; production deployment tests and multi‑model, multi‑adapter evaluations remain necessary.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a transparent, fully archived paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑002) to evaluate a validator‑assisted LLM NetOps pipeline. The observed, reproducible boundary outcome (n11=400, validator_reject_count=0, repair_calls=0) shows that generation semantics and task selection can make a guarded validator empirically inert. We release all artifacts and SHA‑256 manifests so future preregistered runs can (i) adopt independent generation or injected positive controls, (ii) broaden model and adapter diversity, and (iii) calibrate task difficulty to obtain informative estimates of validator benefit. We emphasize: this run does not support production claims for or against validators — it documents a precisely reproducible experimental boundary that informs how to design informative NetOps safety evaluations.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (artifact‑grounded). Human role and autonomy boundary: after an autonomy lock the autonomous system conducted the literature review, experimental design, preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002), execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI‑peer review response, and revision. The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved autonomy boundaries and pre‑lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. LLM(s) and adapter: model=gpt‑5‑mini (used via a hosted NetOps adapter identified as hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Exact initial master prompt(s), system instructions, and generation templates are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865) and in execution/transformation_manifest.json (hash in execution_manifest). Preregistration/freeze: the preregistration CAND‑2026‑002 (frozen before model calls) specified the research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1–H4), primary and secondary estimands, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), per‑intent paired design, analysis plan (McNemar exact test and bootstrap CIs), seeds (bootstrap seed=1729), retry policy, and maximum model calls (800). These elements are archived (preregistration object in execution_manifest). Framework and tools: experiments used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family to call gpt‑5‑mini; deterministic validator implementation, repair template, and emulator scoring harness are archived (execution/execution_log.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json). What was archived: every prompt, provider call, model output, validator decision, tool call, raw execution log, per‑task scoring JSON, and SHA‑256 manifest (execution_manifest lists each file and hash). Technical restarts and failures: the execution_manifest records started_at_utc and completed_at_utc; completed_episode_count=800, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=400. Pre‑lock development: prior infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence; no pre‑lock experimental outcomes were used as final evidence. Post‑run artifacts: analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg) and the analysis log are archived; principal artifact hashes include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf. Important interpretive note required by the run: the preregistered generation_semantics was shared_initial_candidate (one identical candidate generated per paired episode) and the deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0). Consequently the Guarded pipeline was inert in this execution (no repair calls invoked), producing perfect concordance (n11=400). This outcome is fully traceable in the archived artifacts and is reported above as a documented boundary case. All archived artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes are released to enable reproducibility and to allow independent follow‑on preregistered experiments that vary generation semantics, task sampling, or validator configuration.
limitations: Single‑model and single‑adapter: only gpt‑5‑mini with hosted_netops_gvr_v1 was used; results do not generalize to other LLMs/adapters.

Generation semantics choice (shared_initial_candidate) made the Guarded intervention empirically inert in this execution (validator_reject_count=0), preventing the preregistered hypotheses from being tested on these tasks.
Task bank and emulation: public/synthetic intents in sandboxed emulator replicas do not fully represent production heterogeneity or adversarial inputs.

No preserved injected positive controls: archived scoring JSONs show no observed near‑failures, so post‑hoc assessment of scorer/validator false negatives is not possible from the preserved artifacts alone.
Vendor/device fidelity: emulator replicas and vendor models are approximations; broader vendor and hardware validation is required before operational claims.
